scope: Core VP8 RTP repair dependency and original video IO expiry only, local macOS arm64. This does not install or qualify canonical RTC video, NACK/RTX sockets, actual browsers, Linux/remote, acceptance or publication.
implementation: QueuedMedia::deliver_video_with_repair issues an opaque VideoRepair only after the original guarded send returns success. Only a bounded complete VP8 RTP packet with one original source qualifies; generic audio/data remain one-use and no raw payload accessor or public clone is added.

The retained packet keeps original bytes, capture/arrival time, source and target ports, route-generation tickets, source identity and selection/scene stamps. No current policy reader is retained between calls. A transport must bind the handle to that exact original actual sender/wire packet in its bounded cache.

Each explicit repair reacquires ordinary current Core source, target, membership/Endpoint, media, audience, route, gate and selection permission. Four attempts per original packet/recipient share an atomic budget, including refused attempts. There is no automatic retry of uncertain IO.

Non-data delivery now uses the original monotonic arrival plus200ms as its outer IO cutoff. Video previously checked initial age but could then renew pending IO by another200ms. Original delivery and repairs now stop at the same original cutoff; shorter fresh credentials still win.

Current IO is destroyed before its authorization guards release on cutoff or cancellation. Expired/failed/unsupported original delivery returns no repair handle. Existing canonical RTC hosting still refuses video/SCTP pending its adapters.

Canonical reliable data, full synchronized source clocks, wider RTC lifecycle/failure/query/reoffer/credential cases, public browser API replacement, actual Chrome/Firefox forced fallback, Linux/remote hosting, packages and full Gate6 acceptance remain required.
